name: Elbigenalp
kurzbeschreibung: The main town of the Lechtal, featuring a Baroque parish church and renowned Geigenbau-traditions.
beschreibung:
Overview

Elbigenalp is situated at an elevation of 1,039 meters in the central Lech Valley in the district of Reutte, surrounded by the craggy peaks of the Lechtal and Allgäu Alps. Home to approximately 900 inhabitants, this heritage-rich municipality is historically celebrated as the cultural capital of the valley, fondly called the village by locals. Geographically, Elbigenalp is shaped by the untamed River Lech, the vital spine of the Tiroler Lech Nature Park with its broad gravel banks and rare riparian forests. Stately farmhouses decorated with historic baroque frescoes and traditional trompe-l'œil wall paintings bestow a distinctive cultural dignity upon this recognized health resort.

History

The municipality's name stems from an alpine pasture overgrown with elm trees, with records establishing the earliest settlement around 1312 alongside church records. Elbigenalp is world-renowned as the birthplace of Anna Stainer-Knittel (1841–1915), immortalized as the Geierwally. In 1860, the nineteen-year-old artist accomplished the extraordinary feat of rappelling down an abyss in the Saxerwand on a hemp rope to retrieve an eagle's nest, an act of courage that inspired Wilhelmine von Hillern's bestselling novel Die Geierwally. The village's artisanal prestige is anchored by the Elbigenalp Woodcarving School, tracing back to a drawing school founded in 1835 by lithographer Johann Anton Falger; today it operates as Austria's premier college for craftsmanship, sculpture, and design. The parish church of Saint Nicholas features baroque interiors, while the cemetery's Saint Martin Chapel houses the famous Elbigenalp Dance of Death from 1840, presenting eighteen poignant painted wooden panels illustrating human mortality.

Getting There

By automobile from Germany, travel is toll-free without an Austrian vignette via motorway A7 to Füssen, continuing through Reutte along the scenic B198 Lechtal highway into Elbigenalp. From Innsbruck, the route follows motorway A12 and the B179 across the Fern Pass to Reutte; during summer months, the dramatic alpine Hahntennjoch pass road via Imst offers a scenic alternative. From Vorarlberg, visitors arrive via Warth and the Bregenzerwald. Rail passengers arrive at Reutte in Tirol station or Füssen railway terminal. VVT regional bus line 120 runs regular scheduled services connecting Reutte station directly with Elbigenalp. In summer, the specialized Lechtal hikers' bus accommodates bicycles and is free or discounted with the Lechtal Aktiv Card.

Tips

Attending a dramatic summer theatrical performance at the Geierwally Open-Air Stage, built directly into the towering vertical cliffs of Bernhard Gorge, is unforgettable. Trekking enthusiasts walking the famous Lechweg trail enjoy Elbigenalp as an essential staging post. Families will relish a leisurely forest hike up to the traditional Gibler Alm or a tour of the Wunderkammer Elbigenalp museum in the historic physician's residence. Experienced mountaineers can tackle the ascent to Hermann-von-Barth-Hütte at 2,131 meters, the highest alpine shelter in the Northern Limestone Alps. In the village center, open sculpture studios invite visitors to observe master woodcarvers practicing their refined craft.
